subject.title: [Feature]: Add a visible browser panel to the Control UI for login handoff and browser management

question: What security and ownership boundary should the Control UI browser-login handoff surface use before implementation?
rationale: Automation can prove the missing surface from source, but it cannot safely choose how much authenticated browser state the Control UI may reveal or control, nor whether the first implementation is core-owned or plugin-contributed.

options.title: Read-only-first operator handoff
options.body: Expose status, profile, tabs, target context, and screenshots/logs by default, while requiring explicit user intent for navigation, clicks, credential entry, and submit actions.

options.title: Wait for plugin UI entry points
options.body: Defer the browser-specific panel until the generic plugin UI entry-point contract is accepted and implement the browser view as a plugin-owned surface.

options.title: Defer browser UI
options.body: Keep CLI/RPC/browser skill workflows as the supported path until browser handoff becomes a prioritized product area.

recommendation.title: Read-only-first operator handoff
recommendation.body: Expose status, profile, tabs, target context, and screenshots/logs by default, while requiring explicit user intent for navigation, clicks, credential entry, and submit actions.

likelyOwner.reason: He supplied the canonical acceptance criteria in the issue and has the strongest combined signal across browser, Control UI, and product-routing history.
